etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English widwer, equivalent to widow +‎ -er.

definitions.definition: A man whose spouse has died (and who has not remarried); a man in relation to his late spouse; masculine of widow. [from 14th c.]

quote.citation: 1850, [Alfred, Lord Tennyson], In Memoriam, London: Edward Moxon, […], →OCLC, Canto XIII, page 20:
quote.text: Tears of the widower, when he sees⁠A late-lost form that sleep reveals,⁠And moves his doubtful arms, and feelsHer place is empty, fall like these; […]

quote.citation: 1988 April 2, Lori Kenschaft, “Film on lovers of PWAs in works”, in Gay Community News, page 6:
quote.text: What happens to the lovers of people with AIDS? How do they experience the passage from lover to caregiver to "widower"?
